title: Reuse and cleanup
current: Lane lookup uses the public item reference and recorded branches; cleanup acts on a recorded branch, or on detached@<commit> when the checkout has no branch. A done item's lanes retire on the machine that holds them once each proves clean and landed: by ancestry, patch equivalence, or commits that net to no change. A lane several tasks of one epic shared retires once every task finished and the epic is done or cancelled. The standing relay for the machine's active connection (`active_env`) sweeps every checkout that connection maps at start and every 15 minutes on a background thread, logging each lane removed and each lane kept with its reason under `lane sweep:`; any other relay, such as a stage relay beside prod, never sweeps and logs that it is off. Only one sweep runs in a checkout at a time; another skips with `another lane sweep is running in this checkout`. One malformed lane in a prune batch is reported and skipped; the other lanes in that batch are still judged. A clean detached lane whose commit is on the target retires; a dirty or unmerged detached lane stays, with the reason named. A cancelled item's lanes are deleted outright — worktree (even dirty, locked or unmerged), local branch and origin branch — by the cancel on its own machine and by the relay's next lane sweep on every other machine, and each deletion's head SHAs land in the item's Progress Log under `Cancelled lanes deleted`. Every successful machine-wide lane removal also releases its item_worktrees row through item_worktrees.release_merged_lane, including an already-absent directory. A lane folder, named cache, or removal tombstone that disappears after the sweep has read it counts as removed, and the sweep continues with the lanes behind it. This retires finished worker lanes of an open parent without leaving competing active merge sources. An older authority response without item_ref preserves the lane with prune_owner_identity_unavailable and the instruction to update the serving control plane and retry. Preserved folders keep their rows; a failed row release warns with the stranded branch and cause for control-plane recovery. A standalone landing retires the item's own lanes and then runs the machine-wide merged-lane sweep. A deployment run retires no lanes; the relay on each lane's machine sweeps them. `HC-worktree-health` only reports terminal lanes, naming a finished one `verified-safe; the relay's periodic lane sweep removes it`; its `--fix` removes no item lane. `max_worker_lanes` is the machine's only lane limit and is enforced before worker launch. Git worktree count never refuses lane creation; an old `max_active_worktrees` machine setting is ignored. Before creating a lane, creation runs the same finished-lane sweep. `HC-worktree-health` lists landed lanes of open items on their own line while they await release close-out. A lane is disposable when git reports only named caches (including `.hypothesis`) or paths the project declares in `disposable_generated_paths`; any other ignored file preserves it. A checkout with no origin remote (a local-only project) skips the machine-wide sweep with `no origin remote (local-only project)` instead of a remote-refresh warning.
verification: Before cancellation cleanup deletes a lane, its local/remote heads and dirty-path count are recorded through item_worktrees.cancelled_lanes.record in the owning item's Progress Log. Retain partial/not-deleted warnings; the function is the cleanup receipt, not independent deletion authority. This mapping exercises no cleanup.
